newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical says strong dollar cut into results.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical says strong dollar cut into results.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. Thursday reported a drop in profits for the first quarter, and noted that the strong dollar had a negative impact on its results.
It earned $452 million or $1.90 a share compared with year-earlier earnings of $476 million, which also was equal to $1.90 a share. Revenues were flat at $4.99 billion.
Dow said the strong dollar had a negative impact of about $100 million on its sales.
"The strong U.S. dollar played a significant role in the price decline we experienced in the first quarter," said William S. Stavropoulos, president and chief executive officer.
"As we head into the second quarter, favourable global economic conditions will support solid volume growth in our businesses," Stavropoulos said.

"Lower feedstock costs and price stability in some key products, coupled with the on-going implementation of our productivity and value-growth initiatives, should result in a strong quarter for Dow," he said.
Dow's stock was up $1.50 at $81.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
